liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Deal** (1 review): Reviewer calls this Deal a scorcher [7]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Deal slowly transitions into a flawless sixteen-minute Bird Song, which the reviewer says the Grateful Dead never did for them [7]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): John Mayer shone humbly on this song, according to the reviewer [16]
- **Sugaree** (1 review): John Mayer shone on this song too, per the turf-standing reviewer [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Passenger**: rare: 9 archived performances [17]
- **Goin' Down the Road Feelin Bad**: mythic rare: 2 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **deadco2016-07-16.mg21.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 18 songs; 183 min; rated 4.44/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Oteil's bass on the recording is funky, melodic and locked in the pocket [15]
- **deadandcompany2016-07-16.skm140.sunboy.flac24**: source not stated; 18 songs; 187 min [2]
- **deadandco2016-07-16.sony.spyder9.flac16**: source not stated; 18 songs; 183 min [4]
- **DeadCompany2016-07-16**: source not stated; 17 songs; 183 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer, a longtime Dead-show attendee, saw this lineup for the first time; found many highs in the first set and soulful sing-alongs [13]
- Reviewer bought Boston tickets early and watched several summer tour webcasts beforehand [14]
- Reviewer stood on the turf at Fenway; the night before was also a great show [16]
- Guest vocalist Donna Jean Godchaux-MacKay sat in with the band, which also featured Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann on drums [2]
- This was the second night of a two-show Boston run on July 15 and 16, 2016 [4]
- Reviewer attended both Citi Field nights but says this Boston show convinced them the band matches the original Grateful Dead's quality [7]
- Reviewer says the band has grown greatly since last year and since the tour opener, reaching energy comparable to the Grateful Dead [8]
- Reviewer had just attended a show at Alpine the previous week [9]
- Reviewer saw nearly a hundred Dead shows starting in 1980, ending with the 1995 Omni run, and preferred Furthur to The Other Ones [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **deadco2016-07-16.mg21.flac16**: taped by Keith Antaya; transferred by Keith Litzenberger; source: MG21>nBob Actives>nBox Platinum>Sony M10(24/48) [1]. Also: Recorded on-the-stage-line position, section C5, row 8, about ten feet away; converted in Sound Forge Pro 11 to 16-bit/44.1kHz FLAC [1]
- **deadandcompany2016-07-16.skm140.sunboy.flac24**: taped by Steven Weld; transferred by Steven Weld; source: Neumann SKM140(AK40's/LC3's/KM100's)>GAKables xlr>Lunatec V2>GAKables xlr>Apogee Mini-Me@24/48>AES/EBU>Sound Devices 722 @24bit/48kHz [2]. Also: Taped from turf section C5 behind the ninth row, even with the mixer, using Schoeps and DPA microphones on a tall stand [2]
- **deadandco2016-07-16.sony.spyder9.flac16**: taped by Dan Nolan, Jr. - spyder9; transferred by Dan Nolan, Jr. - spyder9; source: AKG C568EB > Shure FP24 > Sony PCM-M10 (24/44.1) [4]. Also: Taped, edited and transferred by Spyder9 Studios from Turf C5, row 8, seat 13 [4]
- **DeadCompany2016-07-16**: taped by Jay; transferred by Jay; source: Source: Schoeps MK4's>Schoeps CMR's>Naiant PFA>Edirol R-44 OCM [6]. Also: Recorded with Schoeps MK4 mics into Schoeps CMR, Naiant PFA preamp and Edirol R-44, about twelve feet away in C5 row 8 [6]
